names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 2 noiembrie, «Sfântul Mucenic Aftonie».
Read out of saint.gr's line for 2 Νοεμβρίου, «Άγιοι Ακίνδυνος, Αφθόνιος, Πηγάσιος, Ελπιδηφόρος και Ανεμπόδιστος», with the rank word left off.
Read out of the title on his name link behind the line for 2 ноября ст. ст., «Аффоний Персидский, мч.», with the rank word left off. The day's own line declines it as «Аффония».

feast.note: His name page lists this day and no other.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 2 ноября ст. ст. — «Мчч. Акиндина , Пигасия , Аффония , Елпидифора , Анемподиста и иже с ними (ок. 341-345).»
source.note: The day's typikon sign is «Совершается служба, не отмеченная в Типиконе никаким знаком» and it hangs on this line, the day's first; the other three lines carry none.

attestations.note: The line's «Мч.» is martyr, which this folder already held. The name page gives him the by-name «Персидский», the Persian, which is the epithet this corpus's English form already carried. The line closes «и иже с ними», and those others — the king's mother and the up-to-seven-thousand Christians of the procession — are named by the life and not by the calendar, so they take no folder.

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 2ης Νοεμβρίου — «Άγιοι Ακίνδυνος, Αφθόνιος, Πηγάσιος, Ελπιδηφόρος και Ανεμπόδιστος»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 2 Νοεμβρίου εκάστου έτους», the same day the folder's Romanian row already carries, and the entry enumerates the same five men the corpus already keeps. A `dates` object is proposed from the page's heading. He is the one of the five the page singles out: Shapur beheaded him first. The two hymns name the five and are taken into all five folders. No asterisk and not the sentence «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη η ύπαρξη του Αγίου».
Not checked: pravoslavno.rs for the corresponding Julian day (25 September 2026).

hymns.text: Purtătorilor de lupte ai Domnului, fericit este pământul care s-a adăpat cu sângele vostru şi sfinte locaşurile care au primit trupurile voastre. Că în privelişte pe vrăjmaşi aţi biruit şi pe Hristos cu îndrăznire aţi propovăduit, pe Acela ca pe un Bun rugaţi-L să mântuiască sufletele noastre.

source.text: doxologia.ro, Troparul Sfinților Mucenici Achindin, Pigasie, Aftonie, Elpidifor și Anempodist, Glasul 2

english.text: Champions of the Lord: blessed is the earth that was watered with your blood, and holy are the shrines that received your bodies. For in the arena you overcame the enemy and preached Christ with boldness. Entreat him, as the Good One, to save our souls.

hymns.text: Ακίνδυνον μέλψωμεν, συν Αφθονίω ομού, κλεινόν Ανεμπόδιστον, Ελπιδοφόρον στερρόν, Πηγάσιον ένδοξον ούτοι γαρ ακινδύνως, εξαφθόνου κρατήρας, πηγάζουσι τοις ελπίδι, αρραγεί προσιούσι, χαρίτων ανεμποδίστων, κρήνην θεόβρυτον.

source.text: saint.gr, Ἀπολυτίκιον (Κατέβασμα), Ήχος δ’, Ταχύ προκατάλαβε — the first hymn on the page of the five. It names all five of them and no other saint.

english.text: Let us sing of Acindynus together with Aphthonius, of famed Anempodistus, steadfast Elpidephoros and glorious Pegasius; for these, without danger, pour out ungrudging bowls, a God-given spring of unhindered graces, for those who come to them with unbroken hope.

hymns.text: Τη της Τριάδος καλλονή λαμπρυνθείσα, η πενταυγής των Αθλητών θεία φάλαγξ, τας των τυράννων ήμβλυνε δεινάς προσβολάς, άφθονον ακίνδυνον, ανεμπόδιστον χάριν, άπασι πηγάζουσα, τοις ελπίδι και πόθω, ενθέως προσιούσι δι' αυτών, τω πάντων Κτίστη, Χριστώ τω Θεώ ημών.

source.text: saint.gr, Κοντάκιον, Ήχος δ’, Ο υψωθείς — on the page of the five. It calls them the five-rayed divine phalanx of the contenders and puns on their names; it names no other saint.

english.text: Made bright by the beauty of the Trinity, the five-rayed divine phalanx of the contenders blunted the dreadful assaults of the tyrants, pouring out for all an ungrudging, danger-free and unhindered grace — for those who through them come with hope and longing, in godly fashion, to the Maker of all, Christ our God.

hymns.text: Страстотерпцы Господни,/ блаженна земля, напившаяся кровьми вашими,/ и свята селения, приимшая телеса ваша,/ в тризнищи бо врага победисте/ и Христа со дерзновением проповедасте:/ Того яко блага молите// спастися, молимся, душам нашим.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 2 ноября ст. ст. — «Тропарь мучеников». The text names none of the five and is the common of martyrs, printed under their line and copied whole, as the brief directs; it is the Slavonic of the troparion these folders already hold in Romanian, and not the Greek one, which puns on all five names.

english.text: Passion-bearers of the Lord, blessed is the earth that drank your blood, and holy are the dwellings that received your bodies; for in the arena you overcame the enemy and preached Christ with boldness. Pray to him, as to the Good One, that our souls may be saved.

hymns.text: Благочестивыя и богоносныя мученики,/ яко на земли оставльшия вся,/ приял еси в наслаждение благих Твоих и упокоение,/ Акиндина, Пигасия, Анемподиста,/ с нимиже Аффония и Елпидифора же,// Едине сый Преблагий.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 2 ноября ст. ст. — «Кондак мучеников». The text names all five men and is theirs; it is not the kontakion these folders already hold in Greek, which is a different composition on the same five names.

english.text: The pious and God-bearing martyrs, who left all things on earth, you have received into the delight of your good things and into rest — Acindynus, Pegasius, Anempodistus, and with them Aphthonius and Elpidephorus — you who alone are most good.

death.note: Two calendars fifteen years apart, and the interval holds both. saint.gr gave «(; - 330)» for each of the five, which these folders carried as a flat 330; days.pravoslavie.ru closes the same company's line «(ок. 341-345)», about 341 to 345, and its life sets the whole story in the reign of «Сапора II (310 - 381)», which contains both readings and settles neither. Nothing is chosen.
